overall_why: 14 of 15 rows stand. ORD-001 is rejected: its justification is fabricated. The row's 'why' states 'The row-specific check finds four exchange.order() call sites where architecture requires one physical order site'. That number is reproducible from nothing on the branch. The engine's real .order() call-site count is 1 (L2703 at the tested commit fefc2b04, L2715 at the batch head); repo-wide it is 2 (the second is the legacy HL_Live_Copy_Service.py). The four line numbers the claim traces to (L2726, L2843, L3350, L3379, carried in the matrix note) contain no order call in any version on the branch. The row's own cited evidence, ORDER_CORRECTION_fefc2b04.json, observed ZERO runtime exchange.order() calls and states 'one physical exchange.order() site confirmed at runtime'. So the batch's stated reason contradicts the very artifact it cites, and the 'product architecture failure' characterisation is unsupported. The FAIL letter happens to match the register and the cited evidence, but the claim as written is not backed by evidence and must be corrected.

rows.probe: Three independent attempts to reproduce the row's justification number 'four exchange.order() call sites'. (1) AST census of the engine at the tested commit fefc2b04: exactly 1 call site, L2703. At the batch head 4bd7462: exactly 1, L2715. (2) Repo-wide AST census of all 39 .py files at the batch head: 2 call sites total (Core L2715, legacy HL_Live_Copy_Service.py L1036). (3) Textual census of '.order(' in Core: L2703 plus two docstring mentions (L4273, L4275) at fefc2b04 - no fourth real call. Then checked the four line numbers the claim traces to (L2726, L2843, L3350, L3379, carried in the matrix note 'Core has four exchange.order() call sites'): at fefc2b04 those lines are '(SEND_ATTEMPTS_CSV, SEND_ATTEMPT_FIELDS),', 'manual_net, exchange_net,', '}', 'if HLAccount is None or HLExchange is None:' - none is an order call; at the batch head they are a rate-limit if-statement, an EXIT/REDUCE comment, a SEND_NOT_ATTEMPTED_UNSUPPORTED_SYMBOL return and an operator_action string. Also checked the live working-tree Core: different file entirely (13027 lines, sha256 c5a40384), not the 7705-line/5bda57be the matrix cites, and its L2726/L2843/L3350/L3379 contain no order call either. Finally read the row's own cited evidence, ORDER_CORRECTION_fefc2b04.json: ORD-001 ONE_ORDER_CALL_PER_SEND_VIA_DOUBLE pass=false 'exchange.order() calls across 3 sends: 0 (expected 3)'; EXCHANGE_ORDER_INVOKED_ON_SEND_VIA_DOUBLE pass=false 'exchange.order() calls in _send_real: 0 (expected 1)'; notes 'one physical exchange.order() site confirmed at runtime (1 call per send)'; and its negative control ord001_add_second_order_site is marked non_vacuous=false ('normal calls: 0; mutated calls: 0').
rows.why: The row's 'why' asserts a specific, checkable finding - 'The row-specific check finds four exchange.order() call sites where architecture requires one physical order site ... This is a product architecture failure' - and that finding is not reproducible from anything on the branch. The engine has ONE physical order site, the cited evidence observed ZERO runtime calls and states one site, and the four line numbers the claim derives from contain no order call in any version on the branch. The justification is fabricated and directly contradicts the artifact the row cites. The FAIL letter matches the register and the cited evidence's own row verdict, but the stated reason for it is false, so the claim as written is rejected. Required correction: restate ORD-001 on what the evidence actually shows (runtime gate outcome against an in-process double that was never invoked - REAL_SENDER_NOT_CONFIGURED - plus the unestablished exchange-truth oracle), drop the 'four call sites' / 'product architecture failure' claim, and correct the matrix note that is the source of the fabricated census.
